//: Optional regional-network overlay. Rename this file to topology.json to enable. Schema documented at web/src/topology.ts.
//1: The example below describes mainland China: 16 ChinaNet/Unicom/Mobile backbone POPs, 17 trunk segments connecting them, and a Beijing↔Shenyang coastal corridor of synthetic hub points so landRoute can step overland instead of cutting across Bohai Bay. Replace with your own country/region's anchors.
//corridorHubs: Tianjin→Tangshan→Qinhuangdao→Shanhaiguan→Huludao→Shenyang. PeeringDB has few facilities along this stretch; without these, Dijkstra prefers a chord across Bohai Bay. Each entry is [longitude, latitude].
//pmtiles: Optional vector basemaps for the settings panel's Map Detail dropdown. 'local' = a small regional tile set (tens of MB), 'country' = a country/continent set (hundreds of MB up to a few GB). Either may be omitted — Off is always available. Build .pmtiles files yourself with tilemaker against a local OSM extract; the repo doesn't ship pre-built tiles (they're gitignored and operator-supplied).
//noTransitCountries: Countries that carry no internet transit: no land-graph edge may cross their territory (borders come from world.geojson ADMIN). Korea↔China therefore rides the real Yellow-Sea cables instead of an overland line through the DPRK.
//noTransitZones: Water bodies land edges must never cross, as [lon,lat] outer rings. The Bohai inner sea: a long k-NN edge can dilute the bay crossing below the land-fraction test, so the bay itself is declared off-limits to land edges. Submarine cables through the zone are unaffected.
